h1: The 6 Best Lawn Mowers Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $500 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lawn mowers under $500, covering 21-inch cordless, 80V self-propelled and gas models, with advice on lawn size and slopes.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is our top pick for a standard flat lawn when you want a full 21-inch deck without gas. The PowerSmart 21-inch rear-wheel-drive gas mower is the best answer for hills. The PowerSmart 22-inch is the widest deck on the list, and the Greenworks 40V is the lightest option for small lawns.
intro: Spending up to $500 opens a choice that cheaper budgets never face: self-propel or not, battery or gas. Many buyers pay extra for drive they do not need on a flat lot, or skip it and regret it on a slope.

We ranked six mowers that all land in the $200 to $500 bucket, working from the spec sheets and what owners describe. Deck width, drive type, power source and what ships in the box decided the order, because a mower that needs a separate battery purchase is not the bargain it looks like.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Mower
products.verdict: A full-width electric deck with the battery kit already in the box.
products.description:
The LM2114 pairs a 21-inch deck with a cordless battery system, and the battery and charger are included. There is no gas and no cord, and the drive is push rather than self-propelled.

It ranks first because it is the only mower here that gives you a standard full-width deck without engine upkeep and without a separate battery purchase. It sits above the Greenworks 80V because it asks you to do the pushing, and that is the tradeoff: less cost and weight on the drive, more effort on the lawn.

Choose it for a standard flat lawn where quiet and convenience beat traction. The caveat is that a push drive is tiring on slopes, so look at the PowerSmart rear-wheel model if your yard is hilly.
products.idealFor: Standard flat lawns where quiet, low-upkeep mowing matters.
products.skipIf: Your yard has hills or you want drive assistance.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Gas Mower for Hills and Medium Yards
products.verdict: Rear-wheel drive traction for yards that are not flat.
products.description:
This is a 21-inch gas mower with a 170cc OHV engine, rear-wheel-drive self-propulsion and a six-position cutting height. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks second because rear-wheel drive keeps traction on an incline, where the EGO's push drive becomes a chore. It beats the steel-deck sibling here because the listing is built around hills and uneven medium yards, which is what the drive is meant to solve.

Buy it if your lot slopes or has uneven patches. The caveat is gas upkeep: fuel, oil and routine engine care come with the territory.
products.idealFor: Hilly or uneven medium yards that need grip.
products.skipIf: You want zero fuel and engine maintenance.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Self-Propelled Gas Mower, Steel Deck
products.verdict: Similar gas power with a steel deck and three ways to handle clippings.
products.description:
A 21-inch steel-deck gas mower with a 170cc OHV engine, rear-wheel-drive self-propulsion, and 3-in-1 mulching, bagging and discharge. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks below the hills model because the two are equipped similarly and the other listing speaks directly to slopes. The steel deck and 3-in-1 system are the differences, giving you a choice of how clippings are handled.

It suits buyers who want a steel deck and the flexibility to mulch or bag. The caveat is that it overlaps heavily with its sibling, so the deck material is the main reason to pick it.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a steel deck and flexible clipping handling.
products.skipIf: You would rather avoid gas engines.

products.name: PowerSmart 22-Inch 170cc Self-Propelled Gas Mower
products.verdict: The widest cut here, with drive, at a lower cost than electric self-propel.
products.description:
A 22-inch deck with a 170cc gas engine and self-propelled drive, with no battery or charging required. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks below the 21-inch PowerSmart models because the listing shows fewer extras, such as no stated height range or clipping system. What it gives back is the widest deck on the list, which trims the number of passes on a medium lawn.

Choose it if width and drive matter more than features. The caveat is the extra inch is a small gain, and it brings the same gas upkeep as the others.
products.idealFor: Medium lawns where a wider deck cuts mowing time.
products.skipIf: You want feature detail like height range or bagging.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Battery power and drive assist, for a higher price.
products.description:
A 21-inch self-propelled mower on an 80V system, with a 4.0Ah battery and charger included. The listing notes it as the highest price on the under-$500 list.

It ranks fifth because the gas PowerSmart models deliver self-propel for less, so you are paying for battery convenience. Against the EGO, the extra money buys drive assistance instead of a push-only deck.

It suits medium to larger lawns where you want drive and no gas. The caveat is cost, and that runtime depends on the single 4.0Ah battery.
products.idealFor: Medium to larger lawns where you want drive without gas.
products.skipIf: You are price-sensitive or want gas-style runtime.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: The lightest mower here, built for small flat lawns.
products.description:
A 16-inch push mower on a 40V system, with a 4.0Ah battery and charger included. The listing calls it the lightest mower in this group.

It ranks last because a 16-inch deck needs the most passes of anything here, and push drive adds effort. Its weight is the point: it is easy to lift, store and move around obstacles.

Buy it for a small, flat lawn, or if you already own Greenworks 40V tools. The caveat is that it is the narrowest deck and not suited to larger yards.
products.idealFor: Small flat lawns and existing Greenworks 40V owners.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is medium or larger.

whatMatters.detail: Self-propelled mowers power their own wheels, while push mowers rely on you. On a flat lawn the difference is small, but on slopes it is large. Check the listing for the words self-propelled and whether the drive is front or rear wheel.
Gas offers unlimited runtime with engine upkeep, and battery offers quiet, low upkeep and limited runtime. Your lawn size decides which wins. Look for engine cc or battery voltage and amp-hours.
Deck width is the cutting swath. A 21-inch deck is a common size, and a 16-inch deck takes noticeably more passes. Compare the inch figure to your lawn size.
Battery mowers vary on whether the battery and charger ship in the box. Buying them separately raises the real cost sharply. Read the listing for included battery details.
Hills and uneven ground need traction, which rear-wheel drive provides. Flat lawns do not. Look for rear-wheel-drive wording if your yard slopes.

faq.q: Do I need a self-propelled mower?
faq.a: On a flat, small lawn, usually not. On slopes or a medium yard it saves real effort. The PowerSmart models and Greenworks 80V offer it.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake at this budget?
faq.a: Buying a bare battery tool or skipping the included kit. All the battery mowers here ship with a battery and charger, so check that before comparing prices.

faq.q: Is battery worth it over gas?
faq.a: For a standard lawn, battery means no fuel or oil and less noise. Gas wins when runtime and slopes matter.

faq.q: Can I use the Greenworks 40V battery elsewhere?
faq.a: It fits the Greenworks 40V tool platform, so owners of those tools can share it. Check compatibility on the listing.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas mower?
faq.a: Keep fuel fresh, change the oil on schedule and clean the deck after mowing. Check the manual for intervals.

faq.q: What if my lawn is bigger than a medium yard?
faq.a: Choose a gas model such as the PowerSmart 22-Inch, or plan for extra battery capacity with a battery mower.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the best fit for most flat lawns. If your yard slopes, the PowerSmart 21-inch rear-wheel-drive model is the better call. The Greenworks 80V suits buyers who want battery and drive, and the Greenworks 40V works for small lawns.
